title: Which single symbol is a coil times a heel?
description: Three Egyptian landmarks are multiplied in pairs, and every answer turns out to be one landmark symbol. The same idea is then checked on two landmarks of the base five system. Keeko's doubt is that a lotus times a coil gives the symbol just after the lotus.
teaching_notes: One idea: landmarks are powers of the base, so a landmark times a landmark adds the powers and gives another landmark. Watch for students who take the next symbol in the row instead of adding the powers.

source: Find 100 × 10, 1000 × 100 and 100 × 1000 in Egyptian numerals, and check 25 × 125 in base 5.
video_script.why: The child sees that multiplying two landmark numbers of a base system gives another landmark, by adding the powers.
video_script.substitution: Write each landmark as a power of the base, add the powers, and read off the landmark.
video_script.anchor: the book's question on the product of two landmark numbers, in the Egyptian system and in base five
video_script.wrong_answer: a lotus times a coil is a finger
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko takes the symbol after the lotus; but 1000 x 100 = 100000, which is two landmarks above the lotus
video_script.payoff_line: The results are a lotus, a tadpole, a tadpole, and in base five an arrow.

final_answer.value: A lotus, a tadpole, a tadpole, and in base 5 an arrow; each product is a landmark
final_answer.spoken: a lotus, a tadpole, a tadpole, and in base five an arrow, and each result is a landmark

hold_back: A lotus, a tadpole, a tadpole, and in base 5 an arrow; each product is a landmark
maths_rules: 100 x 1000 = 100000: 10^2 x 10^3 = 10^5, a tadpole, the same either way round
Keeko's slip: lotus x coil = finger; but a finger is 10000 and 1000 x 100 = 100000
video_script.design: One idea: multiplying landmarks adds their powers. The landmark row with its powers stays on the board while the working fills in below it.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the Egyptian landmark row heel 10, coil 100, lotus 1000, finger 10000, tadpole 100000; the line coil x heel with an empty box

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.row: the Egyptian landmark row appears with the values
marks.ask: the line coil x heel appears with an empty box

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about multiplying Egyptian landmarks.
<bookmark mark='row'/>A heel is ten, a coil is one hundred, and a lotus is one thousand. A finger is ten thousand, and a tadpole is one hundred thousand.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>We must multiply landmarks in pairs. Which single symbol is a coil times a heel?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board with the empty box

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the landmark row written as powers of 10: 10 to the 1, 10 to the 2, 10 to the 3, 10 to the 5

marks.powers: each landmark in the row is rewritten as a power of ten
marks.add: the line multiplying powers of ten adds the little numbers appears

narration: <bookmark mark='powers'/>Every Egyptian landmark is a power of ten. A heel is ten to the power one, and a coil is ten to the power two.
<bookmark mark='add'/>When we multiply powers of ten, we add the little numbers.

marks.given: the three Egyptian multiplications are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one hundred times ten, one thousand times one hundred, and one hundred times one thousand. <bookmark mark='also'/>We also check twenty five times one hundred twenty five in base five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the single symbol for each

marks.find: the words the single symbol for each are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the single symbol for each one.

beats.on_screen: 100 x 10 = 10 to the 2 x 10 to the 1 = 10 to the 3 = 1000

marks.powers: 100 and 10 are written as 10 to the 2 and 10 to the 1
marks.add: 2 + 1 = 3 is written and 10 to the 3 is read as 1000

narration: <bookmark mark='powers'/>Step one, take a coil times a heel. That is ten to the power two times ten to the power one.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Two plus one is three, so we get ten to the power three. That is one thousand, which is a lotus.

beats.on_screen: 1000 x 100 = 10 to the 3 x 10 to the 2 = 10 to the 5 = 100000

marks.powers: 1000 and 100 are written as 10 to the 3 and 10 to the 2
marks.add: 3 + 2 = 5 is written and 10 to the 5 is read as 100000

narration: <bookmark mark='powers'/>Step two, take a lotus times a coil. That is ten to the power three times ten to the power two.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Three plus two is five, so we get ten to the power five. That is one hundred thousand, which is a tadpole.

beats.on_screen: 100 x 1000 = 10 to the 2 x 10 to the 3 = 10 to the 5 = 100000
narration: <bookmark mark='swap'/>Step three, swap the order, a coil times a lotus. Two plus three is again five.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The answer is again one hundred thousand, which is a tadpole.

beats.on_screen: base 5: 25 x 125 = 5 to the 2 x 5 to the 3 = 5 to the 5 = 3125; 25 x 100 = 2500 and 25 x 25 = 625, total 3125

marks.powers: 25 and 125 are written as 5 to the 2 and 5 to the 3
marks.check2: 25 x 25 = 625 and 2500 + 625 = 3125 are written and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='powers'/>Step four, check base five. A hexagon times a circle is five squared times five cubed.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Two plus three is five. We get five to the power five, which is three thousand one hundred twenty five.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Check by multiplying out. Twenty five times a hundred is two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='check2'/>Twenty five times twenty five is six hundred twenty five. Together they make three thousand one hundred twenty five.

beats.on_screen: Answer: A lotus, a tadpole, a tadpole, and in base 5 an arrow; each product is a landmark

marks.land: the words each result is a landmark are written

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The results are a lotus, a tadpole, a tadpole, and in base five an arrow.
<bookmark mark='land'/>Each result is a single landmark.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the landmark row
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's line lotus x coil = finger; the finger is labelled 10000 and 1000 x 100 = 100000 appears beside it; the line is crossed out

marks.doubt: Keeko's line lotus times coil equals finger appears
marks.check: the finger is labelled ten thousand and one thousand times one hundred is written as one hundred thousand
marks.fix: the line is crossed out and the tadpole is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks a lotus times a coil is a finger, the next symbol in the row.
<bookmark mark='check'/>But a finger is only ten thousand, and one thousand times one hundred is one hundred thousand.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The landmark we reach depends on adding the powers, not on the next symbol.
